To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the fuel cycle of a future nuclear power plant should be designed to maximize the mean-variance ratio of the expected net cash flow, b) the fuel cycle should be designed in such a way that it can be adjusted in the future in case of a shift towards a more sustainable energy system and c) a shift towards more sustainability is not necessarily linked to an increase in financial risk.
The fuel cycle of the next generation of Nuclear Energy Systems is a VLIRI, and the decision to invest into a nuclear power plant is a Real Option.
the nuclear energy system is a very risky investment and that the fuel cycle is a key factor for its profitability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the financial and economic evaluation of the nuclear energy systems.
the question, how a nuclear energy system can be assessed in terms of risk management and how this assessment could influence future nuclear energy systems.
financial aspects of nuclear energy systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nuclear energy industry is not yet mature enough to make a decision on the nuclear fuel cycle, as the industry is still learning about the financial risk of its investments and the risk aversion of its investors.
a more diversified nuclear fuel cycle is not a bad thing.
a nuclear energy system with reprocessing and MOX fuel is not more risky than an once-through fuel cycle system, but that it is more cost efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Real Option Modelling is an appropriate tool to evaluate investments into nuclear energy systems and their financial risk.
the thesis has been able to show how the nuclear industry can be seen as a portfolio of real options and that the nuclear fuel cycle can be understood as a portfolio of options.
the thesis is a contribution towards a new decision-making paradigm for the generation industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a more diversified and flexible fuel cycle strategy is a promising way to manage the high level of uncertainty in the nuclear fuel supply chain.
the nuclear fuel cycle is not a linear chain of events, but a complex network of Real Options.
a more diversified fuel cycle is a more efficient way for risk management.
